ai.description: *Cnemaspis anamudiensis* is a small gecko reaching 37 mm SVL. It is brown with a distinct yellow-spotted vertebral stripe and possesses a prominent, pointed snout and keeled ventral scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis anamudiensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, spine-like tubercles along its flanks, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis anamudiensis* is endemic to the high-altitude shola grasslands and rocky outcrops of the Anamalai Hills in the Western Ghats, typically found above 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Cnemaspis anamudiensis* is a diurnal gecko that remains active during daylight hours, foraging for small insects on the rocky surfaces of its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis anamudiensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis anamudiensis* is endemic to the high-altitude shola-grasslands of the Eravikulam National Park in Kerala, India, occurring at elevations above 2,000 meters.
